topics.title: Introduction to Life Drawing: Meaning, Importance, Parts of the Human Body, and Sketching a Full Human Figure | Primary 6 (Basic 6) First Term Week 1 Cultural and Creative Arts
topics.content:
INTRODUCTION TO LIFE DRAWING: MEANING, IMPORTANCE, PARTS OF THE HUMAN BODY AND SKETCHING A FULL HUMAN FIGURE
CULTURAL AND CREATIVE ARTS (CCA)
PRIMARY 6 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 1
THEME -  ARTS AND CRAFTS
PREVIOUS LESSON - First Term, Second Term and Third Term Cultural and Creative Arts Plan Lesson Notes and Scheme of Work for Primary 5 (Basic 5)
TOPIC - INTRODUCTION TO LIFE DRAWING
LEARNING
1. Introduction
2. Meaning and Importance of Life Drawing
3. Main Parts of Human Body
4. Materials for Life Drawing and Steps in Sketching Full Human Figure
5. Simple Human Body Proportions and Safety Rules During drawing
6. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
7. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of life drawing.
2. State the importance of life drawing.
3. Identify the major parts of the human body.
4. List the materials used for life drawing.
5. Sketch a simple full human figure showing the correct body proportions.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about drawing, imaginative and creative drawing, shading, and drawing simple objects.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by introducing life drawing, where pupils observe and draw a real human figure.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Drawing paper
2. Pencils
3. Erasers
4. Sharpeners
5. Ruler
6. Colouring materials (optional)
7. Chart or picture of the human body
8. A volunteer pupil or mannequin for observation
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Have you ever tried to draw a person standing in front of you? Artists carefully observe people before drawing them so that the body shape, posture, and proportions look natural. This type of drawing is called life drawing.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning and importance of life drawing, identify the major parts of the human body, and practise sketching a simple full human figure by observing the correct body proportions.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF LIFE DRAWING
Life drawing is the art of drawing a real person by observing the person’s body shape, posture, and movements carefully.
IMPORTANCE OF LIFE DRAWING
Life drawing helps pupils to:
1. Observe objects carefully.
2. Improve drawing skills.
3. Understand the human body better.
4. Develop creativity.
5. Improve hand and eye coordination.
6. Learn correct body proportions.
MAIN PARTS OF THE HUMAN BODY
The major parts of the human body are:
1. Head
2. Neck
3. Shoulders
4. Chest
5. Abdomen (stomach)
6. Arms
7. Hands
8. Hips
9. Legs
10. Feet
MATERIALS FOR LIFE DRAWING
1. Drawing paper
2. Pencil
3. Eraser
4. Sharpener
5. Ruler
6. Colouring materials (optional)
LESSON 2 - STEPS IN SKETCHING A FULL HUMAN FIGURE
1. Draw a light vertical line as a guide.
2. Sketch the head.
3. Draw the neck and shoulders.
4. Add the chest and abdomen.
5. Draw the arms and hands.
6. Draw the hips, legs, and feet.
7. Check the body proportions.
8. Darken the correct lines and erase unnecessary lines.
SIMPLE HUMAN BODY PROPORTIONS
1. The head is usually the first part drawn.
2. The shoulders are wider than the neck.
3. The arms should reach around the thigh area.
4. The legs are longer than the arms.
5. The feet support the whole body.
SAFETY RULES During THE DRAWING
1. Sit properly while drawing.
2. Use sharp pencils carefully.
3. Keep drawing materials neat.
4. Do not play with drawing tools.
5. Wash hands after the activity.
LESSON 3 - WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. Life drawing is the art of drawing a ______.
A. real person
B. building
C. vehicle
D. tree
2. Which of the following is a material used for life drawing?
A. Plate
B. Spoon
C. Pencil
D. Bucket
3. Which part of the body is usually drawn first in a full human figure?
A. Head
B. Foot
C. Hand
D. Leg
4. Life drawing helps pupils to improve their ______.
A. cooking skills
B. farming skills
C. swimming skills
D. observation skills
5. Which of the following is part of the human body?
A. Roof
B. Tyre
C. Shoulder
D. Window
B. Fill in the Gaps
Complete the sentences using the words in the box: body, head, pencil, body, legs, observation
6. The ______ is usually the first part drawn in a human figure.
7. A ______ is used for sketching.
8. Life drawing helps to improve ______ skills.
9. The human ______ has many different parts.
10. The ______ support the body when standing.
C. True or False
11. Life drawing involves drawing a real object. ______
12. The neck connects the legs to the body. ______
13. An eraser is useful in life drawing. ______
14. Observation is not important in life drawing. ______
15. The feet help to support the body. ______
D. Match Column A with Column B.
Column A - Column B
16. Head - A. Support the body
17. Pencil - B. Top part of the body
18. Feet - C. Careful looking before drawing
19. Life drawing - D. Used for sketching
20. Observation - E. Drawing a real person
ANSWER KEYS
1. A - Real person
2. B - Pencil
3. A - Head
4. D - Observation skills
5. C - Shoulder
6. head
7. pencil
8. observation
9. body
10. legs
11. False
12. False
13. True
14. False
15. True
16. B - Top part of the body
17. D - Used for sketching
18. A - Support the body
19. E - Drawing a real person
20. C - Careful looking before drawing
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that life drawing is the art of drawing a real person by carefully observing the person’s body shape, posture, and movements.
Pupils also learned the importance of life drawing, including improving observation skills, drawing ability, creativity, hand-eye coordination, and understanding the correct proportions of the human body.
Furthermore, pupils identified the major parts of the human body, such as the head, neck, shoulders, chest, abdomen, arms, hands, hips, legs, and feet. They also learned the materials needed for life drawing, including drawing paper, pencils, erasers, rulers, and colouring materials.
Finally, pupils practised sketching a simple full human figure by following the correct drawing steps and maintaining proper body proportions.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction - The teacher displays a picture of a person or invites a volunteer pupil to stand before the class. The teacher asks pupils to observe the person’s body shape, posture, and body parts before introducing life drawing.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the model carefully and identify the visible parts of the body.
Step 2: Meaning of Life Drawing - The teacher explains that life drawing is the art of drawing a real person through careful observation of the person’s body shape, posture, and movements.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of life drawing in their own words.
Step 3: Importance of Life Drawing - The teacher discusses the importance of life drawing, including:
- Improving observation skills.
- Developing drawing skills.
- Understanding body proportions.
- Encouraging creativity.
- Improving hand-eye coordination.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils state the importance of life drawing.
Step 4: Parts of the Human Body - The teacher points to or displays the major parts of the human body:
- Head
- Neck
- Shoulders
- Chest
- Abdomen
- Arms
- Hands
- Hips
- Legs
- Feet
The teacher explains the position of each part in the human figure.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify and name the major parts of the human body.
Step 5: Demonstration of Sketching a Full Human Figure - The teacher demonstrates how to sketch a simple full human figure by:
- Drawing a light guideline.
- Sketching the head.
- Drawing the neck and shoulders.
- Adding the chest and abdomen.
- Drawing the arms and hands.
- Drawing the hips, legs, and feet.
- Checking body proportions.
- Darkening the final outline.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils follow the teacher’s demonstration and sketch a simple human figure.
Step 6: Group Activity - The teacher divides the class into four groups and assigns the following activities:
- Group 1: Explain the meaning and importance of life drawing.
- Group 2: Identify the major parts of the human body.
- Group 3: List the materials used for life drawing.
- Group 4: Sketch a simple full human figure showing the correct body proportions.
Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, draw, and present their assigned activities.
Step 7: Lesson Summary - The teacher reviews the meaning of life drawing, its importance, the parts of the human body, and the steps involved in sketching a full human figure.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation - The teacher asks oral and written questions and assesses pupils’ sketches of the human figure.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the evaluation questions and present their sketches for assessment.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Rhythmic Pattern: Meaning of Rhythm, Types of Rhythm, and Bass Drum Rhythm of the Nigerian National Anthem | Primary 6 (Basic 6) First Term Week 2 Cultural and Creative Arts
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils,
1. Explain the meaning of life drawing.
2. State at least four importance of life drawing.
3. Identify and label the major parts of the human body.
4. List the materials used for life drawing.
5. Sketch a simple full human figure showing the correct body proportions.
6. Demonstrate good observation skills while drawing a real person.
